## Contents
- What identification looks like with no resonance to aim at — a plain low-pass.
- Why a flat in-band drive is the right design when there is nothing to concentrate on.

[![Launch in Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/CaltechExperimentalGravity/system_ident/HEAD?urlpath=lab/tree/docs/examples/03-fabry-perot-cavity.ipynb)  ·  run this page live (no install; the [in-browser demo](interactive.qmd) is instant)

Different physics: an optical cavity is a single-pole low-pass,

$$G(s) = \frac{\omega_c}{s + \omega_c},$$

with the cavity pole $f_c$ setting the bandwidth (DC gain 1). There is no sharp
resonance to aim at — the identification is signal-to-noise limited. We run the same
full diagnostic set as the resonance examples and recover the pole by maximum likelihood
from a 30 %-wrong prior. The interesting twist: even with no peak, the optimal drive is
not flat — the Fisher information about $f_c$ concentrates around the corner, and the
excitation follows it.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Setup — imports, house plot style, cavity & prior"
import sys, pathlib
_p = pathlib.Path.cwd()
for _c in [_p, *_p.parents]:
    for _d in (_c, _c / "docs"):
        if (_d / "sysid_plots.py").exists() and str(_d) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(_d))

import numpy as np
import sysid_plots as sp
from sysid_campaign import run_siso_passes, param_sigmas, param_convergence_series

from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.plant import SuspensionPlant
from system_ident.fisher import parameter_covariance
from system_ident.design.pintelon import prior_robust_excitation
from system_ident.backends.twin import TwinBackend

FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS = 8192.0, 65536, 6        # T_fft = 8 s (> 3/f_min = 3 s), 6 periods
TOTAL = NPERSEG * N_PERIODS / FS
ACT_LIMIT = 1000.0

fc = 100.0                                       # true cavity pole [Hz]
wc = 2 * np.pi * fc
cavity = TFModel.from_zpk(zeros=[], poles=[-wc], gain=wc)              # DC gain 1
prior  = TFModel.from_zpk(zeros=[], poles=[-2 * np.pi * 70.0],
                          gain=2 * np.pi * 70.0)                       # 70 Hz, 30% off

f_all = np.fft.rfftfreq(NPERSEG, 1 / FS)
band  = (f_all >= 1.0) & (f_all <= 1000.0)
freq  = f_all[band]
Pyy, Px_tot = np.ones_like(freq), 1.0

def fc_of(m):                                    # corner frequency [Hz]
    return float(np.min(np.abs(np.roots(np.asarray(m.den, float)))) / (2 * np.pi))
```

## The parameter we're chasing

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Prior vs true"
sp.param_table(
    ["", "f_c [Hz]", "DC gain |G(0)|"],
    [["prior", f"{fc_of(prior):.1f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(prior):.4g}"],
     ["true",  f"{fc_of(cavity):.1f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(cavity):.4g}"]],
    caption="Before measuring (prior is 30 % low)")
```

## 1 — Design the excitation

```{python}
#| label: fig-fp-excitation
#| fig-cap: "Optimal drive and a flat drive of equal total power for a single-pole cavity. With no resonance to aim at, the optimal drive concentrates around the corner frequency, where the pole location is most informative — a far weaker concentration than a resonant plant allows."
#| code-summary: "Optimal drive for a single pole vs flat"
Pxx_opt  = prior_robust_excitation(freq, prior, Pyy, Px_tot, 0.5, n_iter=6)
Pxx_flat = np.full_like(freq, Px_tot / (freq[-1] - freq[0]))
cov_opt  = parameter_covariance(freq, cavity, Pxx_opt,  Pyy, TOTAL)
cov_flat = parameter_covariance(freq, cavity, Pxx_flat, Pyy, TOTAL)
ratio    = np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)) / np.max(np.diag(cov_opt))

sp.excitation_design(
    freq, np.abs(cavity.eval(freq)), np.sqrt(Pxx_opt), np.sqrt(Pxx_flat),
    prior_mag=np.abs(prior.eval(freq)), ratio=ratio,
    annotations=[(fc, "f_c = 100 Hz")]).show()
```

## 2 — Run the campaign

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Run 3 passes of Pintelon–Schoukens refinement"
tw = TwinBackend(SuspensionPlant({"CAV": cavity}, FS),
                 {"C1:EXC": "CAV"}, {"C1:RSP": "CAV"}, fs=FS, sensor_asd=0.09)
hist = run_siso_passes(tw, "C1:EXC", "C1:RSP", prior, fs=FS, nperseg=NPERSEG,
                       n_periods=N_PERIODS, band=band, freq=freq, Pyy=Pyy,
                       px_total=Px_tot, n_passes=3, prior_uncertainty=0.5, seed=0)
final = hist[-1]["model"]
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Parameter evolution: prior → each pass → true"
rows = [["prior", f"{fc_of(prior):.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(prior):.4g}", "—"]]
for h in hist:
    rows.append([f"pass {h['pass']}", f"{fc_of(h['model']):.2f}",
                 f"{sp.dc_gain(h['model']):.4g}", f"{h['frac']:.2e}"])
rows.append(["true", f"{fc_of(cavity):.2f}", f"{sp.dc_gain(cavity):.4g}", "—"])
sp.param_table(["step", "f_c [Hz]", "DC gain |G(0)|", "σ/θ (CRB)"], rows,
               caption="Parameters at each step")
```

## 3 — Is the drive gentle? The measurement time series

```{python}
#| label: fig-fp-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "First ~8 s (two periods) of pass 1: the Schroeder multisine at the cavity actuator (top) and the low-pass output it produces (bottom)."
#| code-summary: "Drive + cavity response, first ~8 s (2 periods)"
idx = np.arange(0, int(8 * FS), 2)               # 2 periods, decimated 2x for display
t = idx / FS
sp.timeseries(
    t, [("drive (cavity actuator)", hist[0]["drive"][idx], sp.SKY)],
    [("cavity response", hist[0]["response"][idx], sp.GOLD)],
    titles=["<b>Drive</b> — cavity actuator (Schroeder multisine)",
            "<b>Cavity response</b> — single-pole low-pass output"],
    motion_unit="response [a.u.]").show()
```

## 4 — Bode: magnitude, phase, and coherence

```{python}
#| label: fig-fp-bode
#| fig-cap: "Magnitude, phase, and coherence after the final pass. The prior places the pole at 70 Hz against a true 100 Hz; the ML fit recovers it."
#| code-summary: "Magnitude / phase / coherence stack"
mask = hist[-1]["mask"]
sp.bode(freq, [
    dict(name=f"true plant (f_c={fc:.0f} Hz)", H=cavity.eval(freq), color=sp.SKY, width=2.6),
    dict(name="measured (±σ)", H=hist[-1]["H_acc"], color=sp.GRAY, mode="markers",
         err=hist[-1]["err_acc"], mask=mask, size=sp.MK_SMALL),
    dict(name="prior (70 Hz)", H=prior.eval(freq), color=sp.RED, dash="dot"),
    dict(name="ML fit",        H=final.eval(freq), color=sp.GOLD, dash="dash"),
], coh=hist[-1]["coh"], coh_mask=mask).show()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Why the coherence falls in the rolloff
Above the pole $|G|$ rolls off as $1/f$, so the response shrinks toward the sensor noise
floor and the per-bin coherence drops — visible in the bottom panel. The ML fit weights
each bin by its measured variance, so those noisy far-from-pole bins are automatically
down-weighted and the fit is dominated by the well-measured region around the corner.
:::

## 5 — Fit residuals

```{python}
#| label: fig-fp-residuals
#| fig-cap: "Normalised fit residuals (measured − fit)/σ against frequency, with their histogram."
#| code-summary: "Normalized residual + histogram"
resid = ((hist[-1]["H_acc"] - final.eval(freq)) / hist[-1]["err_acc"]).real
sp.residuals(freq, resid, mask).show()
```

## 6 — Parameter recovery against the Cramér–Rao bound

```{python}
#| label: fig-fp-recovery
#| fig-cap: "Prior, ML fit, and true value for the cavity pole and the DC gain, with the Cramér–Rao σ as the error bar on each fit."
#| code-summary: "Parameter recovery with CRB error bars"
sig = param_sigmas(final, hist[-1]["cov"], targets=("fc", "gain"))
sp.parameter_recovery([
    dict(label="f_c [Hz]",       prior=fc_of(prior), fit=fc_of(final),
         true=fc_of(cavity), sigma=sig["fc"]),
    dict(label="DC gain |G(0)|", prior=sp.dc_gain(prior), fit=sp.dc_gain(final),
         true=sp.dc_gain(cavity), sigma=sig["gain"]),
]).show()
print(f"cavity pole recovered: {fc_of(final):.2f} Hz "
      f"(error {abs(fc_of(final) - fc) / fc * 100:.2f}%)")
```

## 7 — Drive-safety margins

```{python}
#| label: fig-fp-saturation
#| fig-cap: "Drive peak and RMS per pass against the actuator limit."
#| code-summary: "Drive peak & RMS vs the actuator limit, per pass"
sp.saturation([{"pass": h["pass"], "peak": h["peak"], "rms": h["rms"]} for h in hist],
              limit=ACT_LIMIT).show()
```

## 8 — Convergence — every parameter

```{python}
#| label: fig-fp-convergence
#| fig-cap: "Fractional parameter uncertainty σᵢ/θᵢ per pass for the pole and the gain, against the 5 % stop target."
#| code-summary: "σᵢ/θᵢ vs pass, per parameter"
sp.convergence(param_convergence_series(hist, ["fc", "gain"], ["f_c", "gain"]),
               target=0.05).show()
```

## 9 — Pass-by-pass: the measurement sharpening

```{python}
#| label: fig-fp-passes
#| fig-cap: "Measured FRF and ML fit at each pass, overlaid on the true cavity response."
#| code-summary: "Measured FRF + fit, overlaid per pass"
sp.pass_overlay(freq,
    [dict(meas_mag=np.abs(h["H"]), fit_mag=np.abs(h["model"].eval(freq)),
          mask=h["mask"]) for h in hist],
    np.abs(cavity.eval(freq))).show()
```
